$comment: Speakable text contract for read aloud. Every client runs its production speakable-text function on input.text with input.final and compares the segment list with expected (kind, placeholder, text byte-exact). A message whose final output is empty shows no read-aloud button. Placeholder segments are spoken as localized sentences chosen by placeholderLocale. Clients must also assert prefix stability: for every case, the output of every code-point prefix with final=false is a prefix of the final=true output of the whole text.

output: Output is an ordered list of segments: {"kind":"sentence","text":...} or {"kind":"placeholder","placeholder":"code"|"table"|"math"}.
Input is only the message text (Markdown). reasoningText, tool steps and citation lists are never passed in.
After all lines are processed, a placeholder that directly follows a placeholder of the same kind (no sentence between) is dropped.
lines: Normalize CRLF and lone CR to LF, then split on LF. Every line is its own block; the end of a line is a sentence boundary.
final=true: every line is complete. final=false (streaming prefix): the text after the last LF is the open line; all earlier lines are complete and are processed exactly as with final=true.
Fence and display-math state carries across lines. Only complete lines change that state. The open line never emits a block placeholder.
blockClassification: Repeatedly strip a blockquote marker /^[ \t]{0,3}>[ \t]?/ first (applies inside fences too).
Inside a fence: a complete line matching /^[ \t]{0,3}F{n,}[ \t]*$/ (F = the fence char, n = opening length) closes it; any other line emits nothing.
Inside display math: a complete line containing the closer ($$ or \]) closes it; any line emits nothing.

1. Fence open /^[ \t]{0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$/, except a backtick fence whose rest contains a backtick (that line is a paragraph): complete line emits placeholder code and enters the fence; open line emits nothing.
2. Display math /^[ \t]*(\$\$|\\\[)(.*)$/: complete line emits placeholder math; if the rest does not contain the matching closer ($$ or \]) enter display math. Open line emits nothing.
3. Table line /^[ \t]*\|/: complete line emits placeholder table; open line emits nothing. Only pipe-led tables are recognized.
4. Thematic break or setext underline /^[ \t]{0,3}([-*_=])(?:[ \t]*\1){2,}[ \t]*$/: nothing.
5. Heading /^[ \t]{0,3}#{1,6}(?:[ \t]+|$)/: content is the rest; on a complete line also remove a trailing /(?:^|[ \t]+)#+[ \t]*$/.
7. Otherwise the whole line is paragraph content. Indented code blocks are not recognized.
Content goes through the inline pass (open = this is the open line) and then sentence splitting (blockEnd = line complete and inline pass did not stop at a pending construct).
inline: The inline pass turns content into a sequence u of code points and math placeholders, left to right. Appending: any whitespace code point becomes U+0020 and is skipped when u is empty or already ends with whitespace; removedCodePoints are skipped.

Pending (open line only): whenever a decision needs a code point beyond the end of the open line, stop. Keep what is already in u and treat the line as not ended. With final=true or on a complete line nothing is pending; "beyond the end" behaves as described per construct.

Backslash: \( ... \) and \[ ... \] on the same line are inline math (placeholder math); unmatched \( or \[ appends ( or [. Backslash before ASCII punctuation appends that punctuation. A trailing lone backslash is dropped. Other backslashes are literal.

Inline code: a backtick run of length n closes at the next backtick run of exactly length n; its content is appended literally (whitespace still normalized, removed code points still removed). Unmatched: the run is dropped.

Dollar: $$...$$ on the line is placeholder math; unmatched $$ is dropped. Single $ opens only if the next code point is not whitespace and not an ASCII digit; it closes at the first later $ that is not preceded by whitespace or backslash and not followed by an ASCII digit; the span becomes placeholder math. Otherwise $ is literal.
Image ![label](url): the label goes through the inline pass (alt text); empty alt contributes nothing. ! not followed by a full link is literal.

Bracket [label]: find the matching ] (nested brackets counted, backslash skips one code point). If followed by ( and a matching ) exists it is a link; otherwise label-only. Label matching /^\s*\^/ (footnote) or /^\s*\d+(?:\s*[,，、\-–]\s*\d+)*\s*$/ (citation) contributes nothing; any other label goes through the inline pass. URL is never read. Unmatched [ is dropped.

Angle bracket: if followed by [A-Za-z/] and a > appears before any further <: <http(s)://...> appends the host; an HTML tag /^<\/?([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*)(?:\s[^<>]*)?\/?>$/ is removed (br appends a space). Otherwise < is literal.

Bare URL: h at line start or after a non-letter/number, starting lowercase http:// or https://. It extends over ASCII 0x21..0x7E except < > " `; trailing . , : ; ! ? ' " ) ] } * _ ~ are given back. Appends the host (text after :// up to / ? # :, leading www. removed).

Emphasis: a maximal run of *, _ or exactly two ~. prev = code point before the run (start of line counts as whitespace), next = after the run (end of complete line counts as whitespace). canOpen = next is not whitespace and (char is not _ or prev is not letter/number). canClose = prev is not whitespace and (char is not _ or next is not letter/number). If canOpen, the closer is the first later run of the same char with the same length that canClose; the content between goes through the inline pass. Unmatched opener: dropped. Run that cannot open but can close: dropped. Otherwise literal. A single ~ or 3+ ~ is literal.
Everything else is appended as is. letter/number = Unicode general category L* or N*.
sentences: Scan u from a start s (skip whitespace first). The first closure after s is: a math placeholder (closes before it, then the placeholder is emitted); or a terminator run followed by its closers.

Terminator run = maximal run of weak/strong terminators. A run of only . with length >= 2 is an ellipsis, not a terminator. A single . is not a terminator when the word before it (non-whitespace code points back to s, leading abbreviationOpeners removed, ASCII-lowercased) is one ASCII letter or is in abbreviations.

After the run, skip closers. Strong run: closes after the closers. Weak run (only weak terminators): closes after the closers only if the next item is whitespace, a placeholder, or the end of a block; otherwise scanning continues after the run.
If the run or its closers reach the end of u: a block end closes there; otherwise (line not ended) the sentence waits.

With no closure the end of an ended block closes the sentence. Length cap L = maxSentenceCodePoints: when the closure c satisfies c - s > L, or there is no closure yet and more than L code points from s are known, force a split: at the last whitespace index q in (s, s+L] (sentence is u[s..q)), else at p = s+L moved left while u[p] is a combining mark (general category M*) and p > s+1.
Emitted sentence text: join, collapse spaces, remove a space directly before any terminator, trim. Drop sentences with no letter/number.
placeholderLocale: appLocale(tag): normalize _ to -, compare case-insensitively. zh with Hant/TW/HK/MO -> zh-Hant, other zh -> zh-Hans; pt -> pt-BR; in -> id; otherwise the base language if it is in appLocales, else null.
readingLanguage comes from the platform language detector; the detector itself is not part of this contract.
